published_statement: Eq.(21): 'we obtain sigma_piN = (59.1 +- 1.9 +- 3.0) MeV = (59.1 +- 3.5) MeV' (first error: piN amplitude; second: the low-energy theorem), with sigma_piN = sigma(0), sigma(t) = <N(p')| m-hat (uu + dd) |N(p)>, m-hat = (m_u+m_d)/2. Eq.(24): 'sum_{q=u,...,t} f_q^N = 2/9 + 7/9 (f_u^N + f_d^N + f_s^N) = 0.305 +- 0.009'. (Quoted as READ in sigma-term-scan.json and massform.py:1344-1357.)
published_hypotheses: H1 Cheng-Dashen low-energy theorem D+(0, 2M_pi^2) = sigma(2M_pi^2) + Delta_R, |Delta_R| <~ 2 MeV from a resonance-exchange estimate (eq.(8)); Delta_D - Delta_sigma = -1.8(2) MeV (eq.(12)).

H2 Isospin-violating corrections (pion mass difference, virtual photons; f_2 = -0.97(38) GeV^-1, |f_1| <= 1.4 GeV^-1, eq.(17)) applied both to the scattering lengths and to the low-energy theorem; the isospin limit is defined with the CHARGED pion mass and the proton mass.

H3 Pionic-atom scattering lengths a^{1/2} = 169.8(2.0), a^{3/2} = -86.3(1.8) x 10^-3 M_pi^-1 (eq.(18)); g^2/4pi = 13.7(2); Roy-Steiner equations solved below s_m = (1.38 GeV)^2 with driving terms from existing partial-wave analyses.

H4 Eq.(24): the heavy-quark (c, b, t) contribution is (2/9)(1 - f_u - f_d - f_s), i.e. (2/27)(1 - f_l) per heavy quark (the SVZ trace-anomaly matching; shown in the rederivation to be exactly 2/(3 beta0) with n_l = 3 light flavours, i.e. leading order in alpha_s and in the heavy-quark limit).

H5 Eq.(24): f_s is a lattice input (Junnarkar-Walker-Loud 2013 per the sibling reading), not derived from the Roy-Steiner analysis; the implied value, computed here by inversion, is f_s = 0.0435, sigma_s = 40.8 MeV, with an implied uncertainty of 10.3 MeV if 0.009 is the quadrature of the two inputs.

H6 f_q^N are scalar COUPLINGS, f_q^N m_N = <N| m_q qq |N> for light q, the quantities that enter the Higgs- (or WIMP-) nucleon coupling; the heavy-quark entries are effective couplings obtained through the trace anomaly, not quark-mass contributions to m_N.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. WHAT THE AUTHORS HAD (2015): the modern pionic-atom scattering lengths -- and those are the data that moved sigma_piN from the ~45 MeV of 1991 to 59.1 MeV (the paper traces the shift to 'our modern knowledge of the piN scattering lengths as extracted from pionic atoms', quoted READ in sigma-term-scan.json): a documented case of an earlier result moving when data arrived, in M's favour as a pattern, but it moved an input, not a theorem, and it moved TO this paper. WHAT CAME LATER, each tested: (1) FLAG 2024 sigma_s averages -- the implied 2015 sigma_s (40.8 MeV) sits inside both bands; no change. (2) The 2023 isospin-convention clarification -- -0.29 sigma on the sum; no change to anything the tree concludes, though the tree names neither convention. (3) Lattice sigma_piN at the physical point -- still ~3 sigma contested (FLAG), attributed in 2024-2026 work to lattice excited states (a method gap on the lattice side, not missing experimental data); every lattice combination keeps the sum within 1.2 sigma. (4) Direct lattice charm sigma terms (RQCD 16, ETM 19), which did not exist in 2015: THIS is the one datum that pushes on the result -- the LO heavy-quark charm value implied by eq.(24) (62.1 MeV) sits ~2 sigma below both, and substituting them moves the sum +0.8 to +4.5 sigma of the quoted 0.009. Evidence against over-reading it: ETM 19 carries a 22 MeV error, FLAG itself calls RQCD 16 'consistent with' ETM 19, and the substitution changes the method (lattice charm for LO matching), so it narrows the result to its LO heavy-quark hypothesis rather than refuting it. Having all of this data changes no conclusion the tree draws: C2 needs a coupling sum >= 0.496 and the largest variant is 0.345.
grade_evidence: (a) The statement as used STANDS numerically: eq.(24)'s form is re-derived exactly in sympy from LO trace-anomaly matching, 0.305 and 59.1 are reproduced as the tree prints them (0.30707 row, 6.2945 %), and the tree's recomputations 0.3066 / 0.2944 are reproduced through its own functions. (b) No moved light-quark datum moves the result beyond 1.2 sigma (six variants, 0.2944-0.3084). (c) The tree's load-bearing hypothesis -- a COUPLING, CONTESTED as mass -- is the source's own (H6), retained. (d) NARROWED because eq.(24) holds at leading order in alpha_s and 1/m_Q (2/27 = 2/(3 beta0), n_l = 3, derived here), and the tree states the relation for c, b, t without naming that order (massform.py:347-353, 1806-1813, 1866-1868); its own READ lattice charm values (FLAG-sc, massform.py:1336-1340) sit ~2 sigma above the LO charm value and move the sum by up to +4.5 sigma. A second, smaller unnamed hypothesis is the charged-pion isospin convention (-0.29 sigma). (e) Not WRONG: nothing contradicts the published statement; not DATA-DEPENDENT: no tree conclusion moves (C2 False needs >= 0.496, largest variant row 0.3478; the HRKM row does not set HIGGS_SHARE_LARGEST_ALL). (f) Caveat on the evidence: the source was not re-read in this stage (alphaXiv quota exhausted, arXiv egress-blocked); the quotations rest on the sibling D67 audit's at-source reading and the tree's READ SOURCES, which agree verbatim.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names H4's order at massform.py:347-353 (e.g. 'SVZ, leading order in alpha_s and 1/m_Q; charm LO sits ~2 sigma below the lattice sigma_c it also prints') and names the charged-pion convention of HRKM-21. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a tree conclusion found that turns on the coupling sum below 0.5 (none: C2 is the only one and needs 0.496), or a physical-point lattice sigma_c large enough, with small error, that the charm correction exceeds the tree's use -- still far from 0.496. To WRONG: only a computed contradiction of eq.(24) itself, which the sympy derivation rules out at LO. To upgrade read_status to READ: re-read 1506.04142 at alphaXiv once the quota resets (answer_pdf_queries on eqs.(18),(21)-(24), the N superscript (p/n/average) and the order statement of the heavy-quark relation); that would also settle the p.1 vs p.4 citation of eq.(21) and the size of the p/n split. It could narrow H4's drift further but cannot move the conclusion-level findings, which are computed from READ values.
